title: SR-4.07 memev uses the live hosted services
request: Closes G101: the seed-stage analysis (A8, C7). memev has no built-in licence endpoint (src/cli/licensing.mjs:55-57 reads only --server and MEMEV_LICENSE_URL) and no built-in checkout address (docs/CHECKOUT.md: memev upgrade prints checkout.url from the vault's config), and hosted sync, backup and relay answer that they are not offered yet (src/services/providers.mjs:12). SR-4.02 to SR-4.05 build the services in memev-cloud and SR-5.01 the live checkout, but no contract makes memev use them. The repository still carries no address (docs/CHECKOUT.md says so, and the leak denylist names the company's domain), so a release takes the addresses from release configuration, never from the source. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-4.02, SR-4.03, SR-4.04, SR-4.05, SR-5.01, QL-1.02.

tasks.title: A release knows where the licence server and the checkout are
requirements: the release workflow writes the licence endpoint and the checkout URL into the release tarball it attaches, as a release config file under src/ that only the commands needing it read (license activate, upgrade and task 2's hosted providers), from the repository variables MEMEV_RELEASE_LICENSE_URL and MEMEV_RELEASE_CHECKOUT_URL; no address appears in the repository's text and the leak scan still passes

precedence is --server, then MEMEV_LICENSE_URL, then the vault config, then the release config; a build from a checkout without the release config behaves as today (no address, and the command says none is set)
memev license activate and memev upgrade contact nothing until the person runs them, and no other command reads or contacts these addresses, so the no-telemetry statement stays true
a release whose variables lack either address fails before anything is published

the npm package is the release's own tarball: docs/RELEASING.md publishes the .tgz attached to the tag after checking its SHA-256, and never runs npm publish on the working tree, which carries no release config

the release-config step runs after the tests and the leak scan and before the tarball is built, refuses an empty or non-https value, and writes the file at the path src/cli/release-config.mjs reads, which ships in the tarball and is copied into the installed runtime
every address taken from the release config or the vault config passes the same https check (or plain http to loopback) as --server and MEMEV_LICENSE_URL
memev upgrade reads the checkout URL from the release config when the vault config has none, and nothing copies release values into the vault config

tasks.title: Hosted sync, backup and relay through the live services
requirements: src/services/providers.mjs offers hosted sync, hosted backup and the hosted relay when the licence is valid or in grace and its services include sync, backup and relay respectively (the features sync_hosted, backup_hosted and relay_hosted) and the release config names the service address; each speaks the protocol of SR-4.03, SR-4.05 and SR-4.04, with sync and backup end-to-end encrypted as SR-4.03 requires
without the entitlement or the address each says why it is not available and names the tier that includes it; no provider says it is not offered yet
memev doctor reports each hosted service as off, not entitled, reachable or failing, and contacts a service only when it is on
the release-config step also writes the sync, backup and relay addresses from repository variables and refuses an empty one; the field names equal the keys src/cli/release-config.mjs exports

selectProvider chooses the hosted sync provider for a vault whose config names it, whose licence is valid or in grace and includes sync, and whose release config names the address, so the daemon's own sync tick uses it

memev backup now uploads a backup through the backup provider in use, and memev backup restore, run in a fresh vault and config folder, reproduces every note; memev backup set and status keep working for a git remote
switching remote access on with an entitled licence and the relay address opens the relay connection SR-4.04 defines, through the tunnel code

a hosted provider is accepted only with a verified licence, valid or in grace, whose services include the provider's service; a business licence (services ['team']), an expired licence or a hand-edited one is refused
